title: Trump's Intelligence director releases Russian disinformation on the public
description_short: Trump's Intelligence director releases Russian disinformation on the public
description_medium: On September 29, 2020, Director of National Intelligence John Ratcliffe declassified a Russian intelligence allegation about Hillary Clinton and sent it to Senate Judiciary Chairman Lindsey Graham. The TrumpFile account says the Senate Intelligence Committee had already rejected the claim during its bipartisan inquiry. Democrats and former intelligence officials objected that releasing it could amplify unsubstantiated Russian material during the campaign.
description_long: On September 29, 2020, Director of National Intelligence John Ratcliffe declassified and sent a Russian intelligence assessment to Senate Judiciary Chairman Lindsey Graham. It alleged Hillary Clinton was personally behind an effort to tie Donald Trump to Vladimir Putin and Russia’s hacking of Democratic National Committee material. The TrumpFile account says the Senate Intelligence Committee had already considered and rejected the allegation during its bipartisan inquiry into Russian election interference. Democrats objected that the disclosure placed a discredited foreign-intelligence claim into public debate and could reinforce Trump’s claims about the investigation. The page also reports criticism from former senior intelligence officials. The event was Ratcliffe’s decision to disclose the assessment; the allegation itself was not established as fact. The source records disagreement about whether the release served public oversight or amplified Russian disinformation during the 2020 campaign. The controversy involved both the content and the timing: critics said the disclosure gave official visibility to a claim the Senate panel had rejected.
organization_tags: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
U.S. Senate Select Committee on Intelligence

preserved_fields.title: Trump's Intelligence director releases Russian disinformation on the public
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump's Intelligence director releases Russian disinformation on the public

notes: The linked TrumpFile page supplies the allegation, recipient, prior Senate review and objections. The linked New York Times page returned HTTP 403, so this description relies on the accessible timeline and keeps the assessment attributed rather than treating it as fact.

title: Donald Trump and Don Jr. tap campaign lawyer Jesse Binnall for Swalwell lawsuit
description_short: Donald Trump and Don Jr. tap campaign lawyer Jesse Binnall for Swalwell lawsuit
description_medium: On March 24, 2021, reports said Jesse Binnall, a lawyer for Trump’s 2020 campaign, would represent Donald Trump and Donald Trump Jr. in Representative Eric Swalwell’s lawsuit over the January 6 attack. The suit also named Rudy Giuliani and Representative Mo Brooks. The complaint alleged civil-rights violations and incitement; those were allegations, not findings by a court.
description_long: Representative Eric Swalwell filed suit on March 5, 2021, against Donald Trump, Donald Trump Jr., Rudy Giuliani and Representative Mo Brooks over the January 6 attack on the Capitol. On March 24, TrumpFile reported that campaign lawyer Jesse Binnall would represent the two Trumps. The complaint alleged that the defendants conspired to violate the civil rights of members of Congress and to delay or prevent certification of Joe Biden’s electoral victory; it also invoked local laws against inciting a riot and terrorism. Those accusations were claims in a civil lawsuit, not judicial findings. TrumpFile noted Binnall’s earlier work on the Trump campaign and his association with Sidney Powell, including work on matters involving Michael Flynn and election-fraud advocacy groups. The timeline also said Binnall represented Trump in a separate case brought by Swalwell. The event documented here is the reported choice of counsel and its connection to the campaign’s legal network, rather than a determination about the lawsuit’s merits.
subcategory: Swalwell civil lawsuit and legal representation

preserved_fields.title: Donald Trump and Don Jr. tap campaign lawyer Jesse Binnall for Swalwell lawsuit
preserved_fields.description_short: Donald Trump and Don Jr. tap campaign lawyer Jesse Binnall for Swalwell lawsuit

notes: I read the linked TrumpFile timeline and its CBS link. The timeline supports the reported representation and identifies claims in Swalwell’s complaint; it describes allegations, not a court ruling. The CBS link concerns Donald Trump Jr.’s separate 2017 Russia-investigation counsel and does not support the 2021 Binnall appointment.

title: Trump: Elon Musk launches America PAC, dodgy entity dedicated to reinstalling Trump
description_short: Trump: Elon Musk launches America PAC, dodgy entity dedicated to reinstalling Trump
description_medium: Elon Musk launched America PAC in July 2024 to support Donald Trump’s campaign. TrumpFile also reported that the group collected user data and that Musk took over the @america account on X, but the page provides no details about the data or legal review and says consent from the former account holder was unclear.
description_long: Elon Musk launched America PAC in July 2024 as a group supporting Donald Trump’s presidential campaign. TrumpFile describes an aim of assembling wealthy technology donors, but supplies no donor list or fundraising figures. The same account says the PAC collected user data and that legal observers considered the practice possibly illegal; it does not identify the data, collection method or legal analysis, so the allegation remains unverified here. It also reports that Musk took over the @america account on X to promote the PAC and speculates that the former account holder had not consented; the page says its author contacted the person and had not received a response at publication. These privacy and account-control claims should remain attributed to the timeline. The linked material establishes the PAC’s launch and stated pro-Trump purpose, but does not establish a legal violation or document a regulator’s finding. The title’s “dodgy” label is editorial language, not a factual conclusion.

preserved_fields.title: Trump: Elon Musk launches America PAC, dodgy entity dedicated to reinstalling Trump
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump: Elon Musk launches America PAC, dodgy entity dedicated to reinstalling Trump

notes: I read the linked TrumpFile page. It says America PAC supported Trump and alleges user-data collection and takeover of the @america X handle, but supplies no collection details, legal analysis or response from the former account holder. No legal finding is documented. Proposed correction: retain the PAC launch and attribute unresolved data and account-control claims; remove the unsupported “dodgy” characterization.

title: Social Media Mobilization for Political Violence and Rally Coordination
description_short: Social Media Mobilization for Political Violence and Rally Coordination
description_medium: The linked publisher page identifies a 2025 study titled “Mobilising the Mob: The Multifaceted Role of Social Media in the January 6th US Capitol Attack.” Its page returned HTTP 403 during review, and the packet contains no study text or examples connecting specific Trump posts to operational planning. The existing long description’s claims about coordinated logistics and legal violations therefore remain unsupported.

preserved_fields.title: Social Media Mobilization for Political Violence and Rally Coordination
preserved_fields.description_short: Social Media Mobilization for Political Violence and Rally Coordination
preserved_fields.description_long: Donald Trump systematically used social media platforms to mobilize political violence including January 6 Capitol attack through Twitter consensus building and alternative platforms like Parler, Gab, and Telegram for action coordination, creating comprehensive violence mobilization network that transformed social media from communication tools into systematic terrorism organization and political violence coordination systems. The comprehensive violence mobilization included Trump's Twitter amplification of false election narratives and outrage generation while supporters used encrypted messaging apps and alternative platforms to plan weapons coordination, share intelligence, and organize real-time attack logistics during January 6 insurrection. The political violence coordination extended to systematic use of multiple platform networks where major sites facilitated ideological content dissemination while smaller, less moderated platforms enabled focused planning and coordination of attacks through anonymity and encryption that provided secure environment for terrorism organization. Trump's social media violence violated federal laws against inciting violence while systematically using platform networks to organize domestic terrorism through coordinated mobilization that transformed online political expression into systematic violence planning and execution against constitutional government. The rally violence coordination created unprecedented use of social media for political terrorism while demonstrating systematic approach to violence mobilization that used platform design features including network structure, content moderation policies, and encryption to enable comprehensive attack coordination against democratic institutions. The social media terrorism established Trump's systematic approach to political violence and democratic destruction, demonstrating willingness to use communication platforms for terrorism organization while creating violence mobilization network that transformed social media from information sharing into systematic coordination of attacks against constitutional government and democratic institutions through comprehensive platform manipulation and violence incitement.

notes: I attempted to read the linked Taylor & Francis paper, but its page returned HTTP 403. The packet provides its title only, not findings that tie Trump’s posts to weapons coordination, operational planning or a criminal violation. The populated original long description is retained verbatim in preserved_fields but cannot be used as fact. Proposed correction: describe the study only after its text or a readable abstract is supplied; remove claims of Trump-led logistics coordination unless supported by evidence.
proposed_correction: Social Media and January 6 Mobilization: Claims Need Readable Study Evidence

title: Trump names Russian agent top D.C. prosecutor
description_short: Trump names Russian agent top D.C. prosecutor
description_medium: Donald Trump named Ed Martin acting U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia on January 20, 2025, then nominated him for the permanent role in February. The linked TrumpFile page reports Martin’s appearances on Russian state television and criticism of his qualifications, but it does not establish that he was an agent of Russia.
description_long: Donald Trump named Ed Martin acting U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia on January 20, 2025, and nominated him for the permanent position the following month. TrumpFile reported that Martin, a Republican operative and Stop the Steal supporter, had appeared on RT and Sputnik between 2016 and 2024 without initially disclosing those appearances to the Senate. It noted that the State Department describes the networks as arms of Russian intelligence; that does not establish that Martin worked for Russian intelligence. The timeline also recounts Martin’s 2017 comments on RT questioning Bashar al-Assad’s responsibility for a chemical attack in Syria, and criticism of his prosecutorial qualifications. It cited a statement opposing his nomination signed by more than 100 former assistant U.S. attorneys. These reports help explain scrutiny of Martin’s appointment and nomination. They do not support the headline’s label “Russian agent,” and the linked AP page was unavailable during review. The article’s arguments about suitability remain attributed commentary rather than proof of foreign agency.
subcategory: Acting U.S. attorney appointment and nomination scrutiny

preserved_fields.title: Trump names Russian agent top D.C. prosecutor
preserved_fields.description_short: Trump names Russian agent top D.C. prosecutor

notes: I read the linked TrumpFile page, which quotes reporting about Martin’s RT and Sputnik appearances, his acting appointment, and opposition from former prosecutors. The linked AP page returned HTTP 403. These materials do not establish that Martin was a Russian agent. Proposed correction: title the entry around Trump naming Martin acting D.C. U.S. attorney and the scrutiny of his media appearances and qualifications.

title: ICE/CBP Supremacy and Deputization of National Guard/Local Law Enforcement
description_short: ICE/CBP Supremacy and Deputization of National Guard/Local Law Enforcement
description_medium: An American Friends Service Committee overview describes immigration-enforcement changes including expanded detention, arrests in schools and other sensitive places, and restrictions on asylum at the southern border. It does not document ICE or CBP being elevated above other agencies or broadly deputizing National Guard and local police as asserted in the original description.
description_long: An American Friends Service Committee overview updated in January 2026 describes immigration policies adopted after Trump returned to office. It reports that the administration ended guidance discouraging arrests at schools, hospitals, places of worship and other sensitive locations; closed the southern border to asylum seekers; reinstated the “Remain in Mexico” policy; suspended most refugee admissions; and expanded detention and deportation. These examples concern enforcement and access to asylum. AFSC’s account is advocacy reporting, and its description does not establish every legal or operational claim in the original entry. In particular, the linked material does not say ICE or Customs and Border Protection was raised above other law-enforcement agencies, merged with the Justice Department, or given broad power to deputize National Guard units and local police. It does not substantiate the claimed red-state and blue-state task forces or privatized support roles. The current headline and original medium description therefore overstate what this source documents. A corrected entry should focus on the specific enforcement measures AFSC describes unless orders or jurisdictional records support the larger claims.

preserved_fields.title: ICE/CBP Supremacy and Deputization of National Guard/Local Law Enforcement
preserved_fields.description_short: ICE/CBP Supremacy and Deputization of National Guard/Local Law Enforcement
preserved_fields.description_medium: Trump implemented Project 2025 plans to elevate ICE and CBP above other law enforcement, merging elements of DHS and DOJ and privatizing support roles. ICE/CBP deputized National Guard in red states and local police in blue states for federal immigration raids, creating armed task forces to arrest and detain immigrants nationwide, including in sanctuary cities. Expansion of internment camps and increased border wall funding accompanied this unprecedented federal-local law enforcement fusion.

notes: I read the linked AFSC overview and the Project 2025 background page. AFSC describes enforcement, detention and asylum policies, but neither linked source supports ICE/CBP supremacy, a DHS/DOJ merger, National Guard or local-police deputization, or the claimed task forces. The AFSC article was updated in January 2026, later than the record’s August 2025 end date; the proposed correction should be limited to actions within the record period and supported by specific orders.
proposed_correction: Immigration Enforcement Expansion and Asylum Restrictions; Deputization Claims Unverified
